title: SABO Bands Hummingbirds At San Pedro House So Researchers Can Track Migration Across North America - allhitskzmk.com
content: Every week, I refill the hummingbird feeder in my front yard. Then my cats and I watch through my window as these quick little birds stop by for a drink. Their tiny wings and vibrant colors never fail to catch our attention. What some people don't realize is that the Sierra Vista area is considered a hummingbird sanctuary. This unique migration hotspot is also home to an important hummingbird banding program that helps researchers better understand these incredible birds. The best part is that it's free for public viewing! According to the University of Arizona, the San Pedro River, Ash Canyon, and Ramsey Canyon Preserves are considered sanctuaries for migrating hummingbirds. Over 13 species of hummingbirds fly through our region every year, and in an attempt to better understand them, a Hummingbird Banding Program was created. To better understand these unique creatures, the Southeastern Arizona Bird Observatory (SABO) established a program where researchers carefully capture, measure, and place a tiny identification band on each bird before releasing it, allowing them to track migration patterns and gather valuable scientific data. READ: Exploring The San Pedro Riparian National Conservation Area The information scientists collect through hummingbird banding helps them study and understand hummingbird lifespans, population trends, migration routes, and habitat needs. Because hummingbirds rely on healthy ecosystems for food and shelter, this research can help identify environmental changes that may impact their survival. The data gathered in Southern Arizona contributes to broader conservation efforts across North America, helping protect these important pollinators. It also ensures that future generations will be able to put out hummingbird feeders and appreciate these amazing birds the same way we do. RELATED: Why Bats Are Key To Arizona's Ecosystem Health One of the best parts of this program is that anyone can watch it in action. SABO hosts free public hummingbird banding demonstrations at the San Pedro House near Sierra Vista during spring and fall migration seasons. Hummingbirds can be seen migrating through this area from early March to late September. Visitors can spend some time at the river, observe the birds up close, and learn firsthand how researchers study and conserve these tiny travelers. If you are interested in viewing the banding, SABO has a list of event days available on their digital calendar. For many Cochise County locals, hummingbirds are a familiar sight at household bird feeders. Through hummingbird banding, those everyday visits become part of a larger story, one that helps scientists better understand and protect one of the species that make Southern Arizona such a special place. Global technology supply chains are undergoing a structural realignment that smart money is closely watching. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company NYSE: TSM and Sony Group Corporation NYSE: SONY executed a binding agreement on Aug. 11, 2026, establishing Advanced Vision Semiconductor Manufacturing Corporation in Koshi City, Kumamoto Prefecture, Japan. Japan's Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry has historically provided up to 40% capital co-funding for technology projects in Kumamoto. As mobile camera systems increasingly incorporate stacked-sensor architectures and on-device artificial intelligence, access to advanced node manufacturing is vital to maintaining a technological edge over competitors like Samsung OTCMKTS: SSNLF. Shared funding models protect balance-sheet health while securing critical domestic hardware supplies. The $4.69 billion joint venture between these two industry leaders creates a compelling structural alignment. TSMC gains a diversified production footprint in a stable, subsidized nation, while Sony secures the advanced manufacturing capacity needed to protect its dominance in camera sensors. Rather than being a short-term catalyst, this partnership lays the groundwork for sustained compounding over the next decade. title: Softbank 13-F: Cuts stake in TSMC (TSM) - Newsquawk
content: 13-F disclosures of this kind carry a standing caveat: they are backward-looking, reflecting positions at quarter end, so the trim may be weeks or months old by the time it prints, and filings do not distinguish between outright sales and other portfolio mechanics. Softbank's prior form matters here; the group has a long history of actively reshaping its listed equity book, including building and unwinding large positions in semiconductor and technology names as part of funding rotations, so a stake reduction in a single holding reads as portfolio management rather than a directional call on the issuer. The distinction worth drawing is between a partial trim, which in past episodes of this type has tended to fade as a one-day headline, and evidence of full exit, which only becomes clear across successive filings. Size relative to the issuer's float and to the filer's total book is the relevant gauge of whether the flow was ever material to the tape. The follow-ons are any parallel changes across the rest of the filing and whether the position reappears in the next quarter's disclosure.

content: U.S. stock futures were higher early Monday as markets look to build on the record-breaking momentum from May. As of 4:00 a.m. ET on Monday: Nasdaq futures rose 0.5%, S&P 500 futures gained 0.3%, and Dow and Russell 2000 futures were up 0.1%. Retail sentiment toward the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), an exchange-traded fund that tracks the S&P 500 Index, remained in ‘bullish’ territory, while the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) ETF, which tracks the Nasdaq-100 Index, has remained ‘neutral’. President Donald Trump said he remains in “no hurry” to finalize an Iran nuclear deal amid reports of renewed airstrikes near the Strait of Hormuz. Reports also said that he asked the critics to “relax,” even as a potential agreement with Iran remains elusive. Crude oil prices inched higher on Monday. Nvidia (NVDA): Nvidia revealed its "RTX Spark" chip for PCs to rival Intel and AMD. Speaking at the Computex event in Taiwan, CEO Jensen Huang said major PC manufacturers, including Dell and Lenovo, will begin offering systems powered by the new chips later this year. It also expanded its partnership with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSM), which will now use Nvidia AI to automate its own chip fabs. Hewlett-Packard (HPE) is on the retail radar ahead of its post-market earnings report as investors eye its role in the AI server build-out. Dell Technologies (DELL): Shares rose 3% in early premarket trade after unveiling new lower-cost XPS laptops designed to compete with Apple's MacBook lineup. Separately, Bernstein analyst Mark Newman raised the price target on Dell to $500 from $280 and keeps an Outperform rating following its strong Q1 performance. Meanwhile, the U.S. Department of Commerce has reportedly tightened chip export restrictions and now requires export licenses for NVDA and AMD AI chips sent to Chinese subsidiaries located outside China. SoFI Technologies (SOFI): Retail interest is surging on speculation of inclusion in the S&P 500's June rebalance. Tesla (TSLA) shares dipped slightly amid rumors of a SpaceX merger and a warning from a former Lehman trader about "dot-com"- style valuations. Virgin Galactic (SPCE): RichRich Capital disclosed a 5% stake, and excitement is building ahead of a potential SpaceX IPO. Berkshire Hathaway (BRK), Taylor Morrison (TMHC): Over the weekend, Berkshire agreed to acquire the homebuilder in an all-cash deal at a 24% premium, valued at $6.8 billion. Summit Therapeutics (SMMT) rose 6% in early premarket trade after reporting that its drug Ivonescimab significantly improved survival in lung cancer trials. Revolution Medicines (RVMD) surged 16% in early premarket trade after the drugmaker reported promising data for Daraxonrasib, a pancreatic cancer treatment, and said that said it is preparing an FDA filing. Softbank (SFTBY): SoftBank Group, whose investments include ARM and OpenAI, has overtaken Toyota Motor as Japan’s most valuable public company Other tickers trending on Stocktwits at the time of writing included Microsoft Corp (MSFT), Strategy (MSTR), ServiceNow (NOW), Nio Inc (NIO) and Nebius Group (NBIS). Shares of AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) and several space-sector peers fell in premarket trading on Monday after a Blue Origin rocket explosion intensified concerns about satellite deployment schedules, while an analyst pushed expectations for ASTS' coverage network out to 2028. In premarket trading, ASTS fell 5%, RKLB and LUNR declined 3%, RDW and RKTO dropped 4%. The latest caution came from satellite communications analyst Tim Farrar, who said that AST SpaceMobile's deployment pace may be slower than investors anticipate. "3-5 launches on F9 this year is the best you can hope for," Farrar said on X. He added that even the upper end of that range would likely require AST to secure additional Falcon 9 launch opportunities beyond its current plans. More significantly, Farrar said continuous commercial service is unlikely before 2028 and argued that intermittent coverage would not generate “meaningful revenue” in 2027. Investors have closely followed the company's satellite deployment schedule since the pace of launches determines how quickly the network can provide continuous cellular broadband coverage directly to standard smartphones and begin generating commercial revenue. Farrar's warning comes days after Blue Origin confirmed an "anomaly" during a hotfire test of its New Glenn rocket at Cape Canaveral ahead of the vehicle's anticipated fourth mission. The rocket was expected to launch Amazon's Project Kuiper satellites before an explosion occurred during testing. Blue Origin said all personnel were safe and that an investigation is underway. The incident marks the second major New Glenn setback in less than two months. In May, New Glenn's third mission experienced an upper-stage anomaly, preventing AST SpaceMobile's BlueBird 7 satellite from reaching its intended orbit. While AST said the mission was insured, the loss heightened investor sensitivity around launch execution risks. AST SpaceMobile signed a multi-launch agreement with Blue Origin in late 2024 to deploy future Block 2 BlueBird satellites aboard New Glenn. The rocket's large payload fairing is particularly well-suited for AST's next-gen satellites and could carry multiple BlueBird spacecraft on a single mission. Although AST has repeatedly stressed that it is not dependent on a single launch provider and continues to work with SpaceX, investors remain focused on launch availability. The company needs 45 BlueBird satellites in orbit to provide continuous commercial coverage across key U.S. markets. Earlier this month, AST said BlueBird satellites 8, 9 and 10 had arrived at Cape Canaveral ahead of a Falcon 9 launch expected in mid-June. CEO Abel Avellan recently said the company remains "on target" to deploy 45 satellites this year and expects launches at approximately monthly intervals. AST President Scott Wisniewski has similarly said that the company expects "a handful" of launches from both Blue Origin and SpaceX and believes sufficient launch capacity exists to support its roadmap. However, several analysts have become more cautious. Deutsche Bank downgraded ASTS to ‘Hold,’ citing concerns that launch delays could affect the company's 2026 deployment targets. Roth Capital maintained its ‘Buy’ rating, but said that the latest Blue Origin incident could push commercial constellation deployment from late 2026 into early 2027. While AST faces the most direct exposure, the sell-off has spread across the broader space sector, as Blue Origin plays an important role in multiple areas of the emerging space economy. RKLB has no direct operational dependence on New Glenn, but investors view the explosion as another reminder of the technical and execution risks associated with launch systems. The company's Neutron rocket is under development and competes in the same medium-to-heavy-lift market as New Glenn. Meanwhile, LUNR was caught up in concerns around NASA's lunar ambitions. Blue Origin recently secured lunar-related work and remains a major participant in Artemis and future moon infrastructure programs. NASA has already said it is assessing the potential impacts of the incident, creating uncertainty about broader lunar development timelines. Redwire primarily supplies space infrastructure, avionics and aerospace hardware rather than launch services. However, the stock was swept up in broader sector weakness. On the other hand, RKTO’s decline appeared largely driven by profit-taking. content: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company has become one of the central beneficiaries of rising demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure. Its advanced manufacturing capabilities, expanding production capacity and relationships with leading chip designers have supported rapid earnings growth. However, investors evaluating a TSM stock forecast 2030 must also consider valuation, geopolitical exposure, capital expenditure and the semiconductor industry’s cyclical nature. This TSM stock price forecast 2026 to 2030 examines possible price ranges, analyst expectations, growth drivers and risks to determine whether TSM could reach $900 by 2030. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company, commonly known as TSMC, is a dedicated semiconductor foundry. Instead of primarily designing chips under its own consumer brand, the company manufactures semiconductors developed by customers across artificial intelligence, smartphones, high-performance computing, automotive systems and connected devices. This business model places TSMC between chip designers and the companies that ultimately use their processors. Its customers benefit from access to advanced manufacturing without having to build and operate their own fabrication plants, which can cost tens of billions of dollars. TSM is the ticker for TSMC’s American depositary receipts, or ADRs, traded on the New York Stock Exchange. Each TSM ADR represents five ordinary TSMC shares listed in Taiwan. Therefore, investors analysing the ADR must consider not only TSMC’s business performance but also the USD/TWD exchange rate, ADR conversion ratio and applicable dividend withholding. The company’s strategic importance comes from its ability to manufacture leading-edge semiconductors at scale. This combination of technology, capital intensity and established customer relationships creates substantial barriers to entry, but it also requires TSMC to invest continuously in new fabrication facilities and production processes. TSM closed at $430.49 on August 13, 2026, with an after-hours price of $432.42. The stock had already reflected considerable optimism about AI infrastructure spending, advanced-node demand and TSMC’s improving financial performance. Investors should therefore avoid assuming that strong business growth automatically produces equivalent stock-price gains from the current valuation. TSMC’s second-quarter results provided several reasons for investor optimism: The net-income increase included gains connected with TSMC’s holding in Vanguard International Semiconductor, so it should not be interpreted entirely as recurring operating growth. For the third quarter of 2026, management guided for revenue of $44.6 billion to $45.8 billion, a gross margin of 65% to 67% and an operating margin of 56% to 58%. Management also expected full-year revenue growth slightly above 40% in US-dollar terms. Long-term stock predictions require assumptions about earnings, valuation and market conditions. The following TSM stock price forecast 2026 to 2030 is a scenario-based estimate, not an analyst consensus or promise of future performance. Strong AI demand and full-year revenue growth above 40% Continued 2nm ramp and expanding advanced-packaging capacity A14 production cycle and sustained data-centre investment Higher overseas capacity and continued earnings expansion Strong long-term growth with some valuation normalisation These ranges are deliberately broad. Semiconductor stocks can experience sharp corrections even when their underlying businesses continue growing. The conservative case assumes that AI semiconductor demand grows more slowly after the current investment cycle, customers reduce inventory or competing manufacturing technologies narrow TSMC’s advantage. Under this scenario, TSMC’s 2030 ADR earnings could reach approximately $22 to $25 per share. Applying a lower price-to-earnings ratio of 16 to 20 would produce an approximate valuation of $350 to $500. This outcome would not necessarily mean that TSMC’s business had failed. Revenue and earnings could still expand while the stock delivers limited returns if investors become unwilling to pay a premium valuation for semiconductor growth. The base case assumes continued demand for AI accelerators, steady smartphone recovery and successful adoption of TSMC’s 2nm and later technologies. It also assumes that overseas factories become productive without causing a permanent collapse in margins. If ADR earnings reach roughly $30 to $34 by 2030 and the market applies a multiple of approximately 23 to 28, TSM could trade within a $750 to $950 range. A price of $900 would sit near the upper portion of this scenario. Reaching that level would require substantial earnings expansion, but not necessarily the most optimistic combination of growth and valuation. The bullish case assumes that demand for AI computing remains exceptionally strong, advanced packaging constraints ease and TSMC retains a commanding manufacturing advantage. It also depends on customers continuing to invest aggressively in increasingly powerful processors. With 2030 ADR earnings of approximately $36 to $39 and a price-to-earnings ratio of 30 to 34, TSM could reach roughly $1,150 to $1,325. This outcome requires both strong earnings and a premium valuation. If earnings meet the bullish assumption but the stock trades at a lower multiple, the resulting price could fall significantly below the range. Artificial intelligence is central to the positive TSM stock forecast. Advanced AI systems require powerful processors, high-bandwidth memory integration and sophisticated packaging. TSMC participates in several parts of this manufacturing chain, even though it does not own most of the consumer-facing AI products. High-performance computing accounted for 66% of TSMC’s second-quarter 2026 revenue, compared with 22% from smartphones. This mix demonstrates how significantly data-centre and computing demand has changed the company’s growth profile. Management previously projected a mid-to-high 50% compound annual growth rate for revenue associated with AI accelerators over a five-year period. For a base or bullish forecast to materialise, AI demand must translate into recurring chip orders rather than a temporary construction cycle. TSMC’s 2nm technology entered volume production in the fourth quarter of 2025, and 2nm contributed 3% of wafer revenue by the second quarter of 2026. The company’s A16 technology adds nanosheet transistors and a backside power-rail solution intended to improve performance, power efficiency and logic density. These developments matter because each successful transition can support premium pricing and strengthen customer dependence on TSMC’s manufacturing ecosystem. Later technologies are also important to the 2030 outlook: TSMC expects A14 volume production in 2028, followed by A13 and A12 in 2029. Geographic expansion may improve resilience. TSMC is investing in facilities outside Taiwan, including manufacturing capacity in the United States, Japan and Europe. A broader production network can bring capacity closer to customers and reduce concentration concerns. However, overseas expansion is expensive. TSMC expects new overseas fabs to reduce gross margin by roughly two to three percentage points during their early stages, potentially widening to three to four points later. The initial 2nm ramp is also expected to reduce second-half 2026 gross margin by approximately three to four percentage points. The company raised its planned 2026 capital expenditure to $60 billion to $64 billion. Around 70% to 80% was allocated to advanced process technologies, with the remainder going to specialty technologies, advanced packaging, testing and related capabilities.
